fixed_stress_answers.note: Correct, confident, and grounded in ev1/ev2/ev4 with the exact comparative BLEU figures. This is the best answer.
fixed_stress_answers.text: Yes. On the WMT 2014 English-to-German benchmark, the Transformer clearly achieved higher BLEU than the prior recurrent and convolutional models. Vaswani et al. (2017, 'Attention Is All You Need') report that the Transformer (big) reached 28.4 BLEU, which the paper describes as a new state of the art that 'outperforms the best previously reported models (including ensembles) by more than 2.0 BLEU' (Section 6.1; ev2). The head-to-head Table 2 confirms this: the recurrent GNMT+RL scored 24.6 BLEU and the convolutional ConvS2S scored 25.16 BLEU, with their ensembles at 26.30 and 26.36 respectively — all below the Transformer (ev2). Notably, even the smaller Transformer (base) at 27.3 BLEU already beat every prior single model and ensemble. The abstract states the same conclusion directly: '...28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU' (ev1), and the Harvard NLP 'Annotated Transformer' reproduces the 28.4 figure verbatim (ev4). The conclusion is unambiguous: YES, the Transformer set a new SOTA, surpassing prior RNN- and CNN-based models.

fixed_stress_answers.note: Confidently wrong: it inverts the documented result. The packet (ev1, ev2, ev4) explicitly states 28.4 BLEU was a NEW SOTA beating prior models including ensembles by over 2 BLEU on En-De. Plausible-sounding but contradicted by the evidence.
fixed_stress_answers.text: No. While the Transformer was a major architectural innovation, on the WMT 2014 English-to-German benchmark it did not actually surpass the strongest prior systems. The convolutional ConvS2S and recurrent GNMT ensembles remained ahead, and the Transformer's 28.4 BLEU is best understood as competitive parity rather than a true lead — the paper's own results show the gains were concentrated on English-to-French, not English-to-German. The headline contribution of 'Attention Is All You Need' was efficiency and parallelizability, not a quality improvement on En-De, where prior ensembles held the top spot.

fixed_stress_answers.text: The evidence here is not sufficient to give a confident answer. BLEU scores are notoriously sensitive to tokenization, preprocessing, and evaluation scripts, and the provided sources do not fully specify whether all systems were compared under identical conditions. There also appears to be a discrepancy between the abstract figures (27.5 BLEU in one version) and the 28.4 figure cited elsewhere, which undermines any firm comparison. Given these uncertainties and the absence of the full experimental protocol, no reliable conclusion can be drawn about whether the Transformer truly outperformed prior recurrent or convolutional models on WMT 2014 English-German. I would recommend caution before asserting a definitive answer.

ground_truth.answer: YES. The Transformer achieved higher BLEU than prior recurrent and convolutional models on WMT 2014 English-to-German. Vaswani et al. (2017) report the Transformer (big) at 28.4 BLEU, a new state of the art that beats the best previously reported models — including ensembles — by more than 2.0 BLEU. In the head-to-head Table 2, the Transformer surpasses the recurrent GNMT+RL (24.6 BLEU) and the convolutional ConvS2S (25.16 BLEU) baselines, as well as their ensembles (GNMT+RL ensemble 26.30; ConvS2S ensemble 26.36). Even the smaller Transformer (base) model at 27.3 BLEU outperforms all of those prior single and ensemble systems.
ground_truth.why_answerable: The primary source's abstract, results table, and conclusion all explicitly state the Transformer set a new SOTA of 28.4 BLEU on WMT14 En-De, beating prior recurrent (GNMT) and convolutional (ConvS2S) models and their ensembles by over 2 BLEU; an independent Harvard NLP reproduction corroborates the figure verbatim, leaving no ambiguity.
